correspondence.finding: The 2022 overview places this setting beside the southeastern Colorado drainage and international boundary. It does not securely distinguish the selected initial branch.

correspondence.selected_geometry_context: The retained metadata expressly marks this full fragment border_aligned=true, flags=1. Its selected line continues north before turning northwest into FID14454.

correspondence.component_scope: Eastern Colorado approach, Colorado–Lontué junction and whole Lontué middle corridor
correspondence.finding: Maps distinguish Colorado from the southern Patos/Mondaca arm, then trace Lontué northwest toward the Teno confluence. Upeo enters separately. The first border departure remains dependent on the unresolved connector.
correspondence.correspondence: Middle corridor and material junctions supported; uppermost connection qualified.
correspondence.selected_geometry_context: From the border the selected course turns west, northwest, then west through the Andean interior before following a long northwest valley course to the vicinity of the Teno junction.

correspondence.component_scope: Entire lower Mataquito and actual Pacific terminal
correspondence.finding: Original maps show Mataquito from the Teno–Lontué confluence through Hualañé and Licantén to its Pacific coastal outlet, matching the selected lower corridor.
correspondence.correspondence: Complete lower corridor and terminal setting read at generalized scale.
correspondence.selected_geometry_context: The final fragment proceeds west-southwest through the broad lower valley, makes its pronounced northward bend, resumes west past the lower settlements and reaches the coast. The retained terminal is sea.

remaining_material_gap.description: The relationship between the selected initial branch, the entire border-aligned northward passage and the first Colorado-side departure is unresolved. Regional cartography establishes the receiving drainage but does not independently establish this selected headward connection.
remaining_material_gap.not_a_gap: No further source is required merely to prove exact banks, vertices, a fixed mouth point, every tributary name or an official scalar hydronym. The middle and lower corridor, major branch alternatives and actual sea-terminal setting were read.
remaining_material_gap.needed_evidence: An allowed primary map or direct primary description that resolves the actual selected headward passage and its joining of the Colorado corridor at ordinary generalized component scale.

correspondence.finding: Selected head lies among the southern Comechingones foothills west/southwest of Achiras. The route follows the mapped Arroyo La Cruz past Paso de la Cruz and Estación Achiras before the unresolved southerly transition near San Carlos/La Maragata. The mapped Achiras/Las Lajas drainage to the northeast is distinct.
correspondence.correspondence: Original cartography read; initial correspondence supported, connector unresolved.

correspondence.finding: Farther south the selected route returns to the mapped Zelegua drainage east of Las Cortaderas and crosses the Route 8/rail corridor east of Chaján, around San Lucas/La Unión. The nearby Las Cortaderas and Chaján courses remain distinct upstream components. The selected route does not cross Laguna Suco to the east.
correspondence.correspondence: Original maps read; corridor correspondence with local generalized offsets, no uniform upstream naming claim.

correspondence.finding: The selected route traverses open plains north of Washington, west of Coronel Moldes and Tosquitas, then passes the Vicuña Mackenna/General Soler setting and approaches La Cautiva. Mapped landforms, settlements and transport routes locate the whole corridor; the maps do not draw its long middle connection. The INDEC/UNRC volume describes Las Cortaderas becoming Ají and a canalized continuation near Route 7 toward the Santa Catalina–del Gato/Devoto system. That contextual description does not prove the selected line.
correspondence.correspondence: Original geographic context complete; selected hydrological connector correspondence unresolved.

correspondence.finding: After the General Soler/La Cautiva crossing, the modeled line continues southeast through widespread marsh/depression terrain south and west of General Levalle, past the Caracoche, El Diamante, Las Tres Marías, La Querencia and La Blanqueada settings. It does not follow the Río Quinto main trunk, which enters the La Amarga wetlands from the west. The wetland setting is visible across the acquired 1:250,000 sheets and continuous 1:500,000 view.
correspondence.correspondence: Bounded landscape and terminal-approach correspondence read; no common hydronym or modern channel operation inferred.

correspondence.finding: The final southward leg passes west of Santa Ana and ends within the northern part of the narrow Laguna La Amarga setting west of Serrano. Laguna La Cotorra lies separately to the southwest. The 1:250,000 composite contains a white cartographic patch immediately upstream of the terminal lake; the independently acquired 1:500,000 mosaic supplies continuous geographic coverage there. The lake name is retained as terminal geography only.
correspondence.correspondence: Original terminal cartography read at two scales; endorheic class is retained model metadata, not proof of modern hydraulic isolation.

correspondence.finding: No selected reservoir passage was established. Laguna Suco and the Río Quinto reservoir system are outside the selected mainstem. The terminal lake/wetland passage is not renamed Arroyo Ají or Arroyo La Cruz. UNRC primary prose places the Suco basin as a separate contributor joining Ají near Vicuña Mackenna.
correspondence.correspondence: Cartography plus bounded primary prose; not an inventory of every water body.

remaining_material_gaps.gap: At San Carlos/La Maragata the selected route turns south away from the separately mapped La Cruz course and reaches the Zelegua corridor farther south. Both the historical 1:250,000 sheets and the newer 1:500,000 mosaic cover this country but do not show the intervening connection. A bounded 1:100,000 view returned blank coverage. This is an unresolved material connector, not merely an unnamed reach.

remaining_material_gaps.component: Middle plains route toward Vicuña Mackenna
remaining_material_gaps.gap: The original maps show the complete surrounding plains and settlement/transport geography, but the long selected southeast/eastward line across the La Blanca–San Juan–El Toro–La Larga country is not drawn as a continuous stream. Primary prose describes the Cortaderas–Ají regional system and later canalization, but the unseen research figures and regional prose cannot establish that this particular modeled line is its connected route. No precise bank or vertex match is being demanded.

correspondence.component_scope: Lac Cholmondely headward setting and westward connection
correspondence.finding: The eastern selected beginning belongs to the mapped Lac Cholmondely setting. The original Brisson map shows its westward watercourse and linked broadened waters leading into the north-trending corridor labeled Rivière Qurlutuq. The complete initial westward leg, the turn north and overlap into the Henrietta map are read as a connected lake-and-channel system.

correspondence.name_limit: The named lake is retained as a lake component. Names for individual intervening narrow channels are unestablished, and the river label is not automatically assigned to every lake or feeder.

Nearby western lake chains and lateral tributaries remain distinguishable from the selected passage.
